title: feat(analyze): a body-only save re-analyses the changed files only
body:
Closes #59 · Part of #3 · step 3 of 3 for ADR 0002's facts key (tau-rs/arch-design#116). Steps 1 and 2 were #67 and #69. ## In plain words Until now every save re-analysed the whole project. That was about 400 of the 457–484 ms the watcher measured against the 500 ms budget (ADR 0026). Most saves only change code inside function bodies, and other files can't see a body: Rust spells every signature out, so names and types resolve through declarations. Think of a book whose index lists chapter titles only: rewording a paragraph changes no index entry, so only that page is re-read. So the analyzer now remembers what it last indexed, including a **declaration fingerprint** per Rust file: a hash of its tokens with whitespace, comments and function bodies left out (items declared inside a body are kept). - A save whose changed Rust files keep their fingerprint re-analyses **only those files**; every other file's delta (its saved facts) is carried forward under its new key. - Anything else re-analyses the unit, as before. Steps 1 and 2 made that safe: facts that need another file's body are derived when the tree is assembled (#67), and each delta is named by everything that determined it (#69). **`incremental_equals_cold` is the proof:** after every scripted save, the incrementally updated facts must equal a cold analysis of the same files, byte for byte, whatever the order of the saves. ```mermaid flowchart LR S["save"] --> P{"manifest, Cargo.lock,
.cargo/ or main_bin changed?"} P -- yes --> CM["cargo metadata again"] --> U P -- no --> D{"a changed .rs file's
declaration fingerprint moved,
or a .rs file added / removed?"} D -- yes --> U["re-analyse the unit
Recompute::Unit"] D -- no --> F["walk + resolve the changed files only
carry the other deltas forward
Recompute::Files"] U --> A["assemble: entries, ports, externals,
tables, queues links (#67)"] F --> A ``` | the save changes | what is analysed | smallsvc, from the save (local) | |---|---|---| | a function body, a comment | that file (`Recompute::Files`) | **140 ms** (`recompute_body_only`) | | a migration, a README | nothing walked; a migration's tables read again | — | | a declaration: signature, `use`, impl header, attribute, `macro_rules!`, an item nested in a body | the unit (`Recompute::Unit`) | **378 ms** (`recompute_declaration`) | | a new module file | the unit | 359 ms (`recompute_new_file`) | | *before this PR, any save* | *the unit + `cargo metadata`* | *436 ms (main's `recompute_one_file`, same machine)* | Declaration saves got faster too: `cargo metadata` (100–270 ms here) now runs only when a manifest, the lock file, `.cargo/` or `areas.toml`'s `main_bin` changes; otherwise the unit plan is reused. ## Decisions taken - **What counts as a declaration.** Everything outside function bodies, plus inside a body: - items declared there (a nested `fn`, a `use`, a `macro_rules!`) - `const fn` bodies (a constant evaluated elsewhere can be an array's length) - `const` / `static` initializers Left out: whitespace, comments and doc comments (no fact carries docs), and macro calls inside a body (what they expand to stays local). Why tokens and not a syntax diff: one pass over the tokens, no previous tree to keep, and the rule is the ADR's own list. - **The unit is still read whole on a body-only save.** Its declarations resolve the changed file's names. Parsing smallsvc's 32 files is a few ms, and only the changed files are walked and resolved through rust-analyzer. Re-analysing only the packages a declaration change reaches (instead of the unit) is a later optimisation: it gives the same result. - **When unsure, re-analyse the unit.** Re-analysing too much is always correct; carrying a stale delta is not. These cases all take the unit path: - no previous index (the analyzer was just opened) - a different store - a delta to carry is gone from the store - a changed `.rs` file that isn't valid UTF-8 - **`Analyzer::last_recompute()`** reports `Unit` or `Files([...])`, so tests and the bench assert the path taken, not just the timing. ## Tests - `tests/incremental.rs` — **`incremental_equals_cold`**: - eight kinds of save, then each one undone, compared with a cold analysis after every step: - a body edit - unrouting `/health` (the handler stops being an entry; derived across files) - dropping `SKIP LOCKED` (the outbox stops being a queue) - `connect` turned into a re-export with `main.rs` unchanged - a `use` - an item nested in a body - a migration - a comment Each step also asserts which path the save took. - four of those saves in all 24 orders - a resolved-depth run in release, `#[ignore]`d in `cargo test` and run by CI's budgets job (new step) - nothing changed → nothing re-analysed - `src/decl.rs`: bodies, whitespace, comments, doc comments and in-body macro calls don't move the fingerprint. Signatures, `use`, visibility, attributes, nested items, a `use` or `macro_rules!` in a body, impl headers, `macro_rules!` bodies, `const` values and `const fn` bodies do. - `benches/budgets.rs`: `recompute_one_file` is split into `recompute_body_only` (a body edit in `PayOrder::run`, which must come back as `Files([src/app/pay.rs])` with the new resolved call) and `recompute_declaration` (a new `pub fn`, which must come back as `Unit`). - The whole workspace passes locally, clippy clean. ## Done in #59, checklist - [x] `tree_files` gains a facts key; `file_facts` stored under it; `changed_files` keeps comparing content hashes; `SCHEMA_VERSION` bumped (#69) - [x] pruning of deltas no recorded tree references (#69, retention option A) - [x] package id = git tree id · dependency package trees · `Cargo.lock` blob id · analyzer version + depth (#69). The tau-rs/arch-design#96 inputs join the analyzer string once decided. - [x] body-only save re-analyses the changed files only; a declaration change re-analyses the unit (this PR) - [x] `Table.queue` and an inserter's `queues` link derived at assembly, together with every other fact that needs another file's body (#67) - [x] `incremental_equals_cold` in CI on the fixture pins (this PR) - [x] `recompute_one_file` reports a body-only save and a declaration save separately (this PR) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
